paragraphs.en: Anne shared her philosophy: "I've decided to enjoy this drive. You can usually find joy in things if you decide firmly to do so. Let's not think of the asylum today; just focus on the drive."
paragraphs.zh: 安妮分享她的看法：“我已经决定要享受这次车程。通常只要你坚定地决定从中找到乐趣，就能发现其中的快乐。今天别想着收容所的事了，让我们只专注于这次车程吧。”

paragraphs.en: She spotted a wild rose and marveled, "Isn't it beautiful? Wouldn't it be delightful if roses could talk?" Marilla responded bluntly, "I've never heard of anyone whose hair changed color as they grew older."
paragraphs.zh: 她发现了一朵野玫瑰，不禁赞叹：“多美啊！要是玫瑰会说话该有多好呢？”玛丽拉直截了当地回答说：“我可没听说过有人的头发会随着年龄变色。”

paragraphs.en: Anne sighed, "Another hope lost. I often comfort myself with the line: 'My life is a perfect graveyard of buried hopes.' It sounds so romantic."
paragraphs.zh: 安妮叹了口气，“又一个希望破灭了。我常常安慰自己说：‘我的生活就是一个充满埋葬希望的墓地。’这句话听起来如此富有浪漫色彩。”

paragraphs.en: Marilla replied, "I don't see how that's comforting."
paragraphs.zh: 玛丽拉回答说：“这话听起来并不让人感到安慰。”

paragraphs.en: "Because it makes me feel like a heroine in a book," Anne explained. "I love romantic things, and a graveyard full of hopes fits perfectly. Are we going to the Lake of Shining Waters today?"
paragraphs.zh: “因为它让我觉得自己就像书中的女主人公，”安妮解释说，“我喜欢浪漫的事物，而满是希望的墓地正合我意。今天我们去银湖吗？”

paragraphs.en: "No, we're heading by the shore road," Marilla said.
paragraphs.zh: “不，我们走海岸那条路。”玛丽拉说道。

paragraphs.en: Anne daydreamed, "The shore road sounds lovely. Does it live up to its name? Just saying 'shore road' brought an image to mind instantly."
paragraphs.zh: 安妮沉浸在幻想中：“海岸路听起来真是美妙。它的名字是否名副其实呢？仅仅说出‘海岸路’这三个词，脑海中就立刻浮现出一幅画面。”

paragraphs.en: She also mentioned, "White Sands is pretty but Avonlea is better; it just sounds like music."
paragraphs.zh: 她还提到：“白沙滩挺不错，但埃文利更好；它的名字听上去就像音乐一样悦耳。”

paragraphs.en: Marilla suggested, "Since you're eager to talk, tell me about yourself." Anne replied enthusiastically, "I don't have much to say about myself, but I'd love to share my imagination instead."
paragraphs.zh: 玛丽拉建议说：“既然你这么想说话，那就告诉我你的身世吧。”安妮热情地回答道：“我自己没什么好说的，不过我很乐意分享一下我的想象世界。”

paragraphs.en: Anne sighed and began her story. "I was eleven last March. I was born in Bolingbroke, Nova Scotia.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮叹了口气，开始了她的讲述：“我上个月三月十一岁了。我出生在诺斯托克省的博林布罗克镇。”

paragraphs.en: My father was Walter Shirley, a teacher at the local high school. My mother's name was Bertha Shirley. Walter and Bertha are such nice names, aren't they?"
paragraphs.zh: 我的父亲叫沃尔特·谢里利，是一位当地高中的教师。母亲的名字是伯莎·谢里利。沃尔特和伯莎这样的名字多好听啊，不是吗？"

paragraphs.en: Marilla nodded, feeling it necessary to add, "I suppose a person’s name doesn’t matter as long as they behave well."
paragraphs.zh: 玛丽拉点了点头，觉得有必要补充道：“一个人的名字不重要，只要他们行为端正就行了。”

paragraphs.en: Anne pondered for a moment and replied, "Well, I don't know." She continued, "I read that a rose by any other name would smell as sweet, but I can’t believe it. A thistle or a skunk cabbage wouldn't be as nice, in my opinion.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮思索了一会儿，回答说：“嗯，我不知道。”她继续说道：“我读过一句话，说是玫瑰不管叫什么名字都一样芬芳，但我可不相信。在我看来，刺菜或臭菘肯定没有那么讨人喜欢。”

paragraphs.en: My father could have been good even if named Jedediah, but it would have been tough."
paragraphs.zh: 即便父亲名叫杰迪达希亚，他也完全有可能是个好人，但那可就难说了。

paragraphs.en: Anne's mother was a teacher at the High school until she married her father and gave up teaching. Mrs. Thomas called them a pair of babies and said they were poor like church mice. They moved to a small yellow house in Bolingbroke.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮的母亲在高中任教，直到嫁给父亲后放弃了教职。汤姆太太称他们是一对孩子，并说他们穷得像教堂的老鼠。他们搬到了博林布罗克的一所小黄房子。

paragraphs.en: Anne imagined honeysuckle over the parlor window, lilacs in the front yard, and lilies of the valley by the gate with muslin curtains everywhere.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮想象着客厅窗户外爬满了honeysuckle，前院里种着lilacs，在门口则有lilies of the valley相伴，而到处都是雪纺窗帘。

paragraphs.en: Anne was born there. Mrs. Thomas said she was the homeliest baby ever, but her mother thought otherwise. Anne felt a mother's judgment would be more accurate than a poor woman’s. She wished she could remember calling her "mother."
paragraphs.zh: 安妮就出生在那里。汤姆太太说她是个相貌平平的婴儿，但她母亲却不这么认为。安妮觉得母亲的判断比一个穷苦女人的要准确得多。她多希望能记得自己曾叫过她“妈妈”。

paragraphs.en: Anne died when Anne was three months old due to fever. Her father followed four days later.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮三个月大时因发热去世，父亲四天后也随之而去。

paragraphs.en: Left an orphan, Anne became Mrs. Thomas's responsibility. Nobody wanted her, and it seemed to be her fate. Mrs. Thomas, though poor with a drunken husband, took care of Anne by hand.
paragraphs.zh: 失去双亲的安妮成了托马斯太太的责任。没有人想要她，似乎这就是她的命运。尽管托马斯太太自己也很贫穷，丈夫又是个酒鬼，但她还是亲自照顾起了安妮。

paragraphs.en: Whenever Anne misbehaved, Mrs. Thomas would ask how she could be so bad when brought up by hand, reproachfully.
paragraphs.zh: 每当安妮表现不佳时，汤斯夫人就会责问道她怎么会被养得这么差劲，语气中带着不满。

paragraphs.en: Anne moved from Bolingbroke to Marysville with the Thomases when she was six. She helped care for their four younger siblings but was left behind when Mr. Thomas died in a train accident. Mrs. Thomas struggled and eventually placed Anne with Mrs. Hammond, who lived near a clearing surrounded by stumps.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮六岁时，随汤玛斯一家从博林布鲁克搬到了玛丽维尔。她帮助照顾家中的四个弟弟妹妹，但当汤玛斯先生在一次火车事故中去世后，她被留在了家中。汤玛斯太太生活艰难，最终将安妮送到了汉蒙德夫人那里，汉蒙德夫人住在一片开阔地附近，周围都是砍伐后的树桩。

paragraphs.en: The place was lonely, but Anne’s imagination kept her company.
paragraphs.zh: 这个地方颇为荒凉，但安妮的想象力陪伴着她。

paragraphs.en: Mrs. Hammond had eight children, including three sets of twins. Anne found the constant care for babies overwhelming. She stayed there for two years until Mr. Hammond died and Mrs Hammond split up her family among relatives before going to the States.
paragraphs.zh: 汉莫德太太共有八个孩子，其中包括三对双胞胎。安妮觉得 constantly 照顾婴儿让她感到压力山大。她在那儿待了两年，直到汉莫德先生去世，汉莫德太太才将孩子们分散到亲戚家中，并前往美国。

paragraphs.en: Forced into an asylum at Hopeton due to a lack of other options, she remained there for four months.
paragraphs.zh: 因别无选择，她被迫住进了霍佩顿的一家疗养院，在那里度过了四个月。

paragraphs.en: Relieved to have finished recounting her experiences in a place that didn't want her, Anne sighed. Marilla asked if she had ever attended school as they rode down the shore road.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮松了一口气，终于在不需要她的地方讲完了经历，不禁叹了口气。两人骑车沿着湖边公路前行时，玛丽拉问她是否曾经上过学。

paragraphs.en: Anne explained her educational background briefly. Last year at Mrs. Thomas’s house, she attended school only during spring and fall due to the lack of a nearby school in winter and summer vacations. At the asylum, she read well and knew many poems by heart, including "The Battle of Hohenlinden" and parts of "The Lady of the Lake."
paragraphs.zh: 安妮简要地介绍了她的教育背景。去年在汤姆斯太太家，由于冬季和夏季没有附近的学校，她只有在春秋季才去上学。在疗养院里，她读书读得很好，还背诵了许多诗歌，包括《霍亨林登之战》以及《湖上夫人》的部分章节。

paragraphs.en: Marilla asked if Mrs. Thomas and Mrs. Hammond were kind to Anne. Anne hesitated, her face flushing red with embarrassment. She said they meant to be good but had much to worry about, like a drunk husband and having twins repeatedly.
paragraphs.zh: 玛丽拉问托马斯太太和汉莫德太太是否善待安妮。安妮犹豫了一下，脸涨得通红，显得有些尴尬。她说她们本想做好人，但确实有很多烦心事要操心，比如有个酗酒的丈夫，还有反复怀双胞胎。

paragraphs.en: Marilla did not press further. Instead, she focused on the road as Anne’s words brought pity for the child. Anne's life was marked by hardship—drudgery and neglect.
paragraphs.zh: 玛丽拉没有再追问。她转而注视着前方的道路，安妮的话让她对这个孩子产生了怜悯之情。安妮的一生充满了艰辛——辛劳和忽视。

paragraphs.en: Marilla saw this in her history. Despite being sent back, Marilla considered letting Anne stay with them, thinking she could be trained to speak less.
paragraphs.zh: 玛丽拉在安妮的历史中看到了这一点。尽管安妮被送了回来，但玛丽拉还是考虑让她留下来，认为可以通过训练减少她说话过多的习惯。

paragraphs.en: Marilla mused that while Anne talked a lot, it wasn’t rude or unladylike. Her people might have been nice.
paragraphs.zh: 玛丽拉思索着，虽然安妮话很多，但并不粗鲁或不淑女。她的家庭背景可能还不错。

paragraphs.en: The shore road was wild and lonesome, with scrub firs growing thickly on the right and steep red sandstone cliffs on the left, close enough to the track that a mare might have tried the riders' nerves.
paragraphs.zh: 这条海滨小路荒凉而寂静，右侧长满了密密麻麻的矮松，左侧则是紧挨着道路的陡峭红砂岩悬崖。这些悬崖近在咫尺，几乎让骑马的人感到有些紧张。

paragraphs.en: Anne broke her silence. "Isn't the sea wonderful? In Marysville, Mr. Thomas took us to the shore ten miles away, and I enjoyed every moment, even with the children to look after.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮打破了沉默：“大海真是美妙啊！在玛丽维尔，汤玛斯先生带我们去了十英里外的海岸，尽管要照看孩子们，我也乐在其中。”

paragraphs.en: I dreamed of it for years. But this shore is better than that one."
paragraphs.zh: 我梦想着它好多年了。但这个海岸比那个更好。

paragraphs.en: She gazed at the gulls soaring over the shimmering blue sea. "Wouldn't it be nice to wake up at sunrise, swoop down over the water, and fly all day? And then return to a nest at night?"
paragraphs.zh: 她凝视着翱翔在波光粼粼的蓝海上空的海鸥。“要是能日出时醒来，然后俯冲到水面上飞一整天该有多好？晚上再回到巢中休息。”

paragraphs.en: Ahead was a large house. "That's the White Sands Hotel," said Anne. "Mr. Kirke runs it, but the season hasn't started yet."
paragraphs.zh: 前方是一座大房子。“那就是白沙滩酒店，”安妮说道，“基尔克先生经营着它，但季节还没开始呢。”

paragraphs.en: Anne sighed. "I hoped it wasn't Mrs. Spencer's place. It feels like the end of everything."
paragraphs.zh: 安妮叹了口气。“我本希望不是斯宾塞太太的房子。感觉就像是所有一切的终结。”
